thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming/generate — p99=2.30s (SLO=1.0s), p95=0.92s. Increased streaming stalls and tail latency since 08:11 UTC. Affected shards: gpu-pool-7-[3..5]. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/s/latency?span=15m

alice: ack, I'm on it. pulling kv cache metrics now — suspecting KV slab churn / fragmentation.

raj: timeline: spike at 08:11:24, coincides with a surge from a high-concurrency customer (customer: data-analytics-prod). prefill inflight jumped ~6x while decode slot utilization stayed flat. prefill/decode ratio skew -> heavy eviction.

marta: can we confirm whether eviction rate increased vs allocation failures? me looking at `kv.slab.evictions_per_min` and `kv.alloc.failures`

raj: quick snippets from metrics (08:05 -> 08:20):
```
kv.slab.churn_rate = 0.46
kv.slab.free_frag_pct = 31.2
kv.slab.evictions_per_min = 145
prefill.inflight = 1200
decode.inflight = 140
streaming.stalls_p95 = 1.6s
```
These numbers indicate fragmentation + prefill overwhelming decode slots.

alice: hypothesis: prefill-heavy workload touching many cold keys is fragmenting slabs and causing allocation stalls that block streaming tails. risk: p99 spikes and streaming stalls for other tenants.

marta: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle prefill for that tenant (quick). 2) bump eviction batch size to free larger contiguous slabs. 3) route high-concurrency streams to dedicated pool. I'd prefer 1+3 short term.

alice: applying tenant-level prefill throttle now: `redwoodctl tenants throttle set --tenant data-analytics-prod --prefill-concurrency 6`
(deploy-bot): succeeded: throttle updated — new limit 6.

shiv: I'll flip routing rule to send that tenant to dedicated-gpu-pool-3 as a temporary escape hatch (can handle extra load). patch:
```
if header x-tenant == "data-analytics-prod": route -> dedicated-gpu-pool-3
```
(traffic-router): rule applied.

raj: monitoring: 08:17 p99 dropped to 1.35s, p95 stable at 0.88s. streaming stalls count halved. good signal but tail still occasionally spikes.

marta: tail spikes likely from tiny free fragments causing more evictions under burst. longer-term fix: slab coalescing + prefill backpressure on allocator. but we need a fast remedial step: rolling restart of 2 nodes in gpu-pool-7 to compact slabs / reclaim fragmentation.

alice: scheduled restart of nodes gpu-pool-7-3 and gpu-pool-7-4, doing sequentially. planning 2-min drains, restart, check p99.

raj: logs during restart showed short-term increase in latency (expected) but after bringing node back p99 down to 0.92s and streaming stalls near baseline.

marta: confirmed: `kv.slab.free_frag_pct` dropped from 31.2 -> 12.1 after restarts. `kv.slab.evictions_per_min` down to ~40.

alice: mitigation summary: 1) tenant prefill throttle applied (concurrency 6). 2) temporary routing to dedicated pool. 3) sequential restarts of 2 nodes to defragment slabs. All three reduced p99 under SLO.

incident-bot: Incident severity: Sev-2 -> customer impact limited (some requests degraded for ~12 minutes).

alice: handing off to next oncall (@oncall-next). Handoff summary: cause = KV cache fragmentation + prefill/decode imbalance from high-concurrency tenant; mitigations applied (throttle, route, restarts); current status: p99=0.92s, p95=0.86s, streaming stalls near baseline.

alice: action items (followups):
- add automatic tenant-level prefill backpressure when prefill/decode ratio > 5
- implement slab coalescing in allocator (medium term)
- add dashboard alert for `kv.slab.free_frag_pct > 25%` + sustained evictions
- run post-incident eval for customer and notify account team

oncall-next: ACK, will monitor for 2 hours, keeping routing rule and throttle in place. I'll prepare a short postmortem with timeline and metrics. please add any logs/notes to the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.internal/3619004321

marta: quick note — we should also test quota-based prefill gating in staging to reproduce.

alice: thanks everyone. closing live triage but leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
